definitions.explanation: Tending to speak little; reserved in speech. Describes a personality trait of not talking much.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{無口|むくち}な{人|ひと}で、{会議|かいぎ}でもほとんど{話|はな}さない。
examples.english: He's a quiet person and hardly speaks even in meetings.

examples.japanese: {無口|むくち}だけど、{仕事|しごと}はきちんとやる{人|ひと}だ。
examples.english: He's taciturn, but he does his work properly.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{無口|むくち}で、{家|いえ}でもあまり{話|はなし}をしなかった。
examples.english: My father was a man of few words and didn't talk much even at home.

notes:
USAGE:
Describes a personality trait rather than temporary silence.
・{無口|むくち}な{人|ひと}/{性格|せいかく} (a quiet person/personality)
・{無口|むくち}になる (to become quiet - e.g., after something happens)

NUANCE:
Generally neutral to slightly negative. Unlike "quiet" in English, {無口|むくち} specifically refers to not speaking much, not to being calm or peaceful.

CONTRAST:
・{無口|むくち} ↔ おしゃべり (taciturn ↔ talkative)
・{無口|むくち} ↔ {饒舌|じょうぜつ} (taciturn ↔ loquacious - more formal)

KANJI BREAKDOWN:
・{無|む} (without) + {口|くち} (mouth) = without [use of] mouth → not talkative
